engineering.title: The indicator must reply with the enclosure lid open and closed
fields: Opening or closing the enclosure must leave the indicator and rear connector usable with the selected cable clip.
The same indicator reply is present with the lid open and closed, and the clip leaves the rear port accessible.
Compare the lid-open and lid-closed reply log with the clip and rear-port views.
Center and offset clips for the indicator lead

engineering.title: Every display segment must remain distinguishable through the window
fields: The window must preserve the whole display row in the recorded viewing conditions, including the warmed card.
Compare the visible segments through each insert with the bare card and check whether reflections hide a segment in the alternate view.
Read the last segment on the bare card and through each insert at the two recorded conditions.
Clear and smoked inserts for the display window

engineering.title: The sample tray must keep its indexed position without marking its edge
fields: Contact with the tray stop must preserve both the position used to locate the next sample and the condition of the tray edge.
The before-and-after views must preserve the tray index and leave its contact edge free of a new scuff.
Compare the tray index and edge marks before and after motion for both stops.
Rigid and soft stop faces on the sample-tray stand

engineering.title: Selecting the left socket must return the left camera image
fields: Socket selection must identify the physical camera even when both plugs have the same external shape.
Each selection opens its own reference image, and both plugs remain accessible with the guide fitted.
Compare the selected socket with the reference image returned for each plug guide.
Symmetric and keyed plug guides for the camera reader

engineering.title: The desk display must follow the reference on warming and cooling
fields: The probe pocket must maintain useful contact with the probe as the direction of the temperature change reverses.
The comparison must cover both directions with the probe seat identified; agreement on warming alone cannot answer the cooling question.
Compare the display and reference curves for the loose and seated probe in each recorded direction.
Loose pocket and spring seat for the display probe

engineering.title: Replay the selected recording when one recorder has produced several files
fields: The replay lookup must identify the recording independently of the name shared by files from the same recorder.
Choosing recording B must reproduce B’s sample sequence, even when recording A names the same recorder.
Compare the replayed samples with the distinct source sequences in recordings A and B.
Replay selection by recorder name or by capture-manifest entry

engineering.title: Only compare frames that can be traced to the same source frame
fields: The image reader must use source-frame identity to distinguish a true pair from two unrelated files with the same name.
Two identical filenames with different source keys must remain distinct. A missing key must leave a frame visibly unpaired.
Inspect the source keys behind each proposed frame pair and the unpaired legacy image.
Frame matching by filename or by source-frame key

engineering.title: Read the carrier direction after motion with the cover fitted
fields: Someone inspecting the assembled carrier must be able to identify its direction in the retained after-motion view.
The direction mark must remain identifiable in the assembled view. A hidden mark cannot support a claim about how far the carrier turned.
Compare arrow visibility on the rim and face in the retained before-and-after images.
Rim arrow and face arrow on the carrier

engineering.title: The lid must stay seated and leave its latch witness visible
fields: A stop that steadies the lid must still let the reader see whether the latch has seated.
The archived views must show both lid witness stripes retaining their positions and show the latch mark with the pad fitted.
Compare the two lid-stripe positions and latch visibility in the cover images.
Hard lid stop and removable felt stop pad

engineering.title: The counter must record a deliberate press and ignore a passing sleeve
fields: The guard must distinguish deliberate use of the counter from contact by clothing.
The same guard must distinguish the two interactions. A deliberate count from one guard and a rejected brush from another cannot establish that.
Compare recorded counts for a deliberate press and a sleeve brush on the same guard.
Flush and raised guards for the desktop counter

engineering.title: Lamp readbacks must identify the correct port without trapping either plug
fields: The reader must prevent left/right ambiguity while still allowing the user to disconnect the chosen port.
Left and right labels follow their own ports, and the collar leaves enough access to remove the plug.
Read the port labels in both mappings and inspect the removal-access view.
Interchangeable reader plugs and keyed collar

engineering.title: Keep the outer display segment visible as the board warms and cools
fields: The board support must keep the visible display within its front opening across the retained warm and cool conditions.
Compare the segment with the mask in place on both archived conditions; the clip must also keep the board registered side to side.
Compare the outer segment at the mask on the warm and cool display frames.
Fixed edge clip and floating clip for the display board

engineering.title: The drawer must stay latched yet open without snagging its finger recess
fields: The specimen drawer needs a positive catch in the motion comparison and clearance for normal opening afterward.
The same tab must remain in the catch after the recorded motion and clear the recess when the drawer opens.
Compare the latch position after motion and the tab’s clearance in the opening view.
Short and long catch tabs on the specimen drawer

engineering.title: The readout must identify which input changed
fields: The displayed label and value must follow the same input. One channel changing must not make the other appear to change.
Changing input B independently of A must affect the B indication. A disconnected input must not be assumed to have a measured state.
Compare the changed reference input with the corresponding displayed channel.

engineering.title: The sample-pot lid must seat consistently at its corner
fields: The chosen insert must allow the empty pot lid to return to a consistent corner seat across closures.
A corner image and comparative loss record must refer to the same insert and closure. One closure per insert cannot establish repeatability.
Compare the corner views and relative loss records belonging to the same closures.
Flat and compliant inserts for the sample-pot lid

engineering.title: Light must stay in its own indicator opening across the comparison
fields: The light guide must keep an illuminated indicator identifiable without spill into the adjacent opening.
The intended opening and its neighbor must be visible in both the warmed view and the return-to-room view of the same guide.
Compare the illuminated opening and its neighbor in the warm and return views.
Unsupported light guide and guide with a spacer

engineering.title: The holder must keep the card aligned and its printed datum readable
fields: The fixture must retain the card in a position a reader can interpret from its printed datum.
Compare the card corner before and after motion and verify the datum can be read in the same retained configuration.
Compare the card corner positions and visibility of the printed datum on each holder.
Center clip and two-edge clip for a reference card

engineering.title: Each selector position must indicate a single input
fields: The recorder user must be able to identify the selected input without the indication alternating while the selector is at rest.
At the left and right positions the recorded display names only the selected input.
Read the input label at the two recorded selector positions for each plate.
Free selector and two-position detent plate

engineering.title: The overlay grid must identify the selected corner cell
fields: A highlighted checkerboard cell must refer to the same location on the removable grid.
The printed grid and highlighted reference checkerboard cell agree at both archived corner selections.
Match the visible grid highlight to the checkerboard cell for both recorded corner selections.
Rotatable and keyed overlays for the preview display

engineering.title: Keep the reference patch visible without masking the adjoining swatch
fields: The shade must permit a reader to compare the reference patch with the swatch beside it in a warmed image.
The reference patch and the boundary of its neighbor remain distinct on the same warmed reader image.
Compare the reference patch and neighboring swatch in the warmed images through each shade.
Opaque and vented shades around the sample reader

engineering.title: A label card must keep both corner references and remain removable
fields: The fixture must retain a repeatable card position without making it impossible to change the teaching example.
Both corner marks stay indexed after the archived motion, and the card can be withdrawn with the same pin arrangement.
Compare both corner marks on the card and inspect the removal view for the paired pins.
Single and paired index pins on the card jig

engineering.title: The readout cable must clear the moving cover and removable panel
fields: Opening the cover or removing the panel must not trap the cable serving the indicator.
The indicator replies in both lid positions and the panel can be withdrawn with the cable clip fitted.
Compare the open and closed reply entries alongside the panel-withdrawal record.
Cable clip on the hinge lid or stationary half

engineering.title: The cradle must seat on all four corners while keeping its index marks aligned
fields: The instrument cradle must sit steadily without losing its recorded position relative to the two marks.
After the recorded bench movement the comparison shows corner seating and both cradle index marks.
Inspect corner seating and both index marks in the post-motion views of the cradle.
Original cradle feet and compliant replacement foot

engineering.title: One key selection must return only that key’s label
fields: The guide must keep the neighboring key clear when either key is selected by itself.
The separate left and right selections each return one corresponding key label.
Compare the individual key selections with the returned labels from both guides.
Raised edge and flush guide for adjacent switch keys

engineering.title: Keep the complete display visible behind either mask
fields: The same carrier should locate either display mask without obscuring the outer character.
Both mask outlines leave the outer character inside the visible opening on the same carrier drawing.
Overlay the two mask outlines on the same carrier drawing and compare the outer character at the opening.
Common carrier or separate carriers for two display masks

engineering.title: Keep one viewing reference for both instrument layouts
fields: A layout comparison should retain a common viewing reference while leaving both instruments’ corner markers visible.
Each layout drawing exposes its corner marker relative to the same marked viewing reference.
Locate the corner marker and the viewing reference on each jig drawing before comparing the two layouts.
Fixed viewing frame or interchangeable insert on the comparison stand

engineering.title: Keep the alignment reference when the legend is removed
fields: The legend panel should be exchangeable without losing its alignment reference on the fixed display.
The concept drawing identifies the same fixed reference with the panel removed and seated.
Trace the same fixed mark in the seated-panel and removed-panel views of the concept drawing.
Alignment mark on the removable panel or the fixed frame

engineering.title: Mounting bracket sits flush and its holes line up
fields: The bracket shall seat against the mounting face without interference and align with the attachment holes.
Compare the LK-014 rework entry with its filed fit photo. Check which mating face and attachment holes the observation identifies.
The installed bracket sits flush with the mating face and the attachment holes align.

engineering.title: Bracket fasteners remain accessible with the cover fitted
fields: The bracket fasteners shall remain accessible with the cover installed.
Bench fixture assembly notes · Cover access
Review the fitted-cover view of LK-014 alongside the fastener-access note for that installation.
Each fastener head is visible and reachable with the cover in place.

engineering.title: Fixture ID is readable with the cover fitted
fields: The fixture identifier shall remain readable with the bracket and cover installed.
Bench fixture identification notes · Label placement
Read the complete identifier in the fitted-cover photograph and match it to the bench article register.
The complete identifier can be read with the cover in place.

engineering.title: Cover witness marks remain visible
fields: The cover witness marks shall be visible in the assembled fixture record.
Compare the joint close-up with the assembled-cover photo requested in the LK-016 traveler. Record which view was supplied.
The assembled-cover photograph shows the witness marks.

engineering.title: Fixture identification stays readable
fields: The fixture identifier shall remain readable with the cover in place.
Read the LK-021 label in the assembled fixture photo alongside the witness marks.
The complete identifier is readable in the assembled fixture photo.

engineering.title: Match the serial in the readout header to the assembly traveler
fields: The readout must identify the same fixture that the traveler names, even if the archived session still uses an older name.
Match the serial in the LK-022 session header with the serial on its traveler.
The two records name the same fixture identifier.

engineering.title: Harness witness tag readable at support
fields: The harness witness tag shall be readable at the support interface with the cover fitted.
Read the full HI-003 support tag in the handoff photograph and compare it with the support entry.
The retained frame shows the support and its full witness tag.

engineering.title: Read the whole witness mark through the fitted cover
fields: The retained photo must show the marked surface through the assembled cover opening. A photo of the loose cover establishes only where the opening is.
Locate the inspection mark in the HI-006 photograph with the cover fitted. Identify any portion hidden by the cover.
The assembled-cover image shows the access witness.

engineering.title: Carrier identity visible at panel handoff
fields: The handoff record shall identify the installed carrier from the assembled panel view.
Read the carrier tag beside the installed RM-010 panel in the handoff view.
The handoff photograph shows the carrier and full identifier.

engineering.title: Identify the optics tray from its own tag in the assembly photo
fields: The reviewer must be able to read the tag on the tray beside its bracket without using the neighboring support to identify it.
Compare the retained tray photograph with the identity recorded in the handoff.
The assembled tray image shows the tag and its bracket in the same view.

history.title: Requirement recorded
history.note: The assembled tray image shows the tag and its bracket in the same view.

engineering.title: Detector cover label stays visible with harness routed
fields: The assembled-view record shall show the detector cover label beside the routed harness and identify the same article as the traveler.
Compare the assembled photograph with the article and cover identifiers in the traveler.
The retained photograph shows the cover label beside the routed harness. A matching export header establishes the article identity only.

history.title: Requirement recorded
history.note: The installed-view image shows the detector label beside the routed harness.

engineering.title: Show the frame mark beside the carrier ID in the assembled panel photo
fields: The handoff image must identify which carrier is fitted to the frame and show the mark specified on the panel record.
Locate the carrier ID and the panel witness together in the assembled RM-012 frame.
An assembled view shows the panel witness and the carrier ID.

history.title: Requirement recorded
history.note: An assembled view shows the panel witness and the carrier ID.

engineering.title: Panel clearance witness visible after assembly
fields: The assembled side view shall show the panel-rail witness through the revised viewing opening.
Use the RM-016 side view to locate the named rail witness beside the panel.
The assembled side view shows the witness on the panel rail.

history.title: Requirement recorded
history.note: The assembled side view shows the witness on the panel rail.

engineering.title: Identify the fixed locator face from its permanent mark
fields: The comparison photograph must identify which face of the fixed locator is visible without relying on the handwritten arrow.
Identify the fixed face from the LG-030 coupon mark, then compare it with the annotation on the sheet.
The comparison image identifies the fixed-locator face without relying on a handwritten arrow.

history.title: Requirement recorded
history.note: The comparison image identifies the fixed-locator face without relying on a handwritten arrow.

engineering.title: Show the movable locator face and its reference face together
fields: The reviewer must be able to establish the movable locator’s orientation from the two faces of the same coupon in one image.
Locate the movable face and its reference in one LG-031 image; identify any edge outside the crop.
The comparison sheet identifies the movable face and the reference face in the same view.

history.title: Requirement recorded
history.note: The comparison sheet identifies the movable face and the reference face in the same view.

engineering.title: Cradle retention indicator visible at handling handoff
fields: The record for the pilot cradle shall show its article tag and indicator face together.
Inspect the archived handoff image for both the article tag and the indicator face.
The handoff image shows the retention indicator and the article tag together.

history.title: Requirement recorded
history.note: The handoff image shows the retention indicator and the article tag together.

engineering.title: The repeat cradle’s export names its own serial
fields: The export header must identify the individual repeat cradle. Its shared Rev A design cannot distinguish it from the pilot cradle.
Compare the serialized cradle tag in the traveler with the retained export header.
The offline export header agrees with the repeat cradle tag in the traveler.

history.title: Requirement recorded
history.note: The offline export header agrees with the repeat cradle tag in the traveler.

engineering.title: Cradle inspection witness visible behind guard
fields: The retained assembled view shall make the guarded cradle witness identifiable in context.
Inspect the archived assembled view for the witness and its guard in the same frame.
The assembled-view image shows the inspection witness with the guard present.

history.title: Requirement recorded
history.note: The assembled-view image shows the inspection witness with the guard present.

engineering.title: Keep the rehearsal dataset with the setup sheet used for it
fields: A reader opening the dataset from the rehearsal index must be able to retrieve the setup sheet for the same article.
Follow the dataset reference from the rehearsal index to the setup record for this article.
The offline archive index identifies the rehearsal dataset and its associated setup record.

history.title: Requirement recorded
history.note: The offline archive index identifies the rehearsal dataset and its associated setup record.

engineering.title: Replay export identifies the recorder and the original recording
fields: A reader must be able to follow the export’s reference to the original recording in the capture manifest and match the recorder serial there.
Follow the export’s capture reference to the manifest and compare the article identifiers.
The export identifies the recorder and cites the manifest entry for the original recording used for replay.

history.title: Requirement recorded
history.note: The local export identifies the capture source retained in the archive manifest.

engineering.title: Index the signed packet by serial and revision
fields: The review index shall name the same article and revision as the build packet.
Open the indexed packet and compare its printed serial and Rev A designation with the index entry.
The linked packet opens for the serial and revision printed in the index. Two packets may have the same descriptive title.

history.title: Archive requirement baselined
history.note: The review index shall name the same article and revision as the build packet.

engineering.title: Signature belongs to the indexed cover edition
fields: The review index shall identify the signed archive cover for the article under review.
Read the edition on the signed page beside the named Pūriri cover. A signature from an earlier packet cannot establish receipt of the current edition.
The signature page identifies the same article and packet edition as the cover named in the handoff index.

history.title: Archive requirement baselined
history.note: The review index shall identify the signed archive cover for the article under review.

engineering.title: Cover-access finding links to one retained photo
fields: The cover-access observation shall reference the exact image retained in the archive.
Follow the witness entry to the Fern integration photo and compare the article and revision in its caption.
The witness entry opens the image for the same article and record revision.

history.title: Archive requirement baselined
history.note: The cover-access observation shall reference the exact image retained in the archive.

engineering.title: Cradle witness receipt identifies the source document
fields: The receipt must identify the document that supplied the cradle witness entry and the article it describes.
Compare the cradle tag, edition and source on the retained witness entry with its archive receipt.
The entry and its archive receipt identify the same article, record revision and source.

history.title: Archive requirement baselined
history.note: The cradle record shall identify the witness entry and identify its origin in the archive.

engineering.title: Image manifest identifies the article and archive revision
fields: The imagery manifest shall identify the article and archive revision used for the handoff.
Look up the camera manifest by article and revision. Check the signed manifest header if the camera nickname finds several entries.
The archive index opens the manifest for the same article and revision.

history.title: Requirement baselined
history.note: The imagery manifest shall identify the article and archive revision used for the handoff.

engineering.title: Signed cover names its authoring source
fields: The review index shall retain the provenance of each signed handoff cover.
Compare the authoring source on the signed cover with the Kiwi index; distinguish the source from the desk that received the file.
The cover and index identify the same serial and authoring source.

history.title: Requirement baselined
history.note: The review index shall retain the provenance of each signed handoff cover.

engineering.title: Recorder export uses the serial on the signed handoff
fields: The recorder archive shall use the serial label from the handoff packet.
Read the recorder serial on the signed handoff and find it in the export index. Keep any development alias as a separate label.
The same article label appears in the export index and signed handoff.

history.title: Requirement baselined
history.note: The recorder archive shall use the serial label from the handoff packet.

engineering.title: Receipt identifies one recorder export edition
fields: The archive receipt shall identify the exact version of the retained export.
Use the receipt’s version and source to distinguish the Kākā exports when their filenames match.
The receipt resolves to one archived version and names the authoring source.

history.title: Requirement baselined
history.note: The archive receipt shall identify the exact version of the retained export.

engineering.title: Cover inspection links to the photo of that article
fields: The inspection packet shall identify the cover witness image retained for the article.
Open the named Mātātā cover photo from the packet and read the article label in that image.
The named source opens one image with the matching article label.

history.title: Requirement baselined
history.note: The inspection packet shall identify the cover witness image retained for the article.

engineering.title: Review packet identifies the source trace and article
fields: The review packet shall cite the archived trace and identify the subject of the observation.
Match the observation label and revision on the Mātātā review sheet with the trace in the referenced archive.
The packet and archive agree on the observation label and record revision.

history.title: Requirement baselined
history.note: The review packet shall cite the archived trace and identify the subject of the observation.

engineering.title: Signed inspection sheet names the individual article
fields: The witness index shall retain the inspected article label and the signed inspection sheet.
Open the signed Miro inspection sheet and compare its serial with the indexed article. A build-group name alone does not identify the unit.
The index opens the signed sheet for the same recorded article.

history.title: Requirement baselined
history.note: The witness index shall retain the inspected article label and the signed inspection sheet.

engineering.title: Indexed inspection receipt matches the article revision
fields: The review index shall identify the inspection receipt from the applicable revision.
Check the revision on the signed attachment receipt against the Miro review index. Keep the previous receipt accessible under its own reference.
The attachment receipt identifies the revision cited in the review index.

history.title: Requirement baselined
history.note: The review index shall identify the inspection receipt from the applicable revision.

engineering.title: Keep a file receipt separate from a review decision
fields: The trial worksheet shall distinguish an archive receipt from an approval record.
Read the document type on the Rātā index entries and distinguish receipt of a file from approval of its contents.
The comparison indexes receipts and approvals as separate record kinds.

history.title: Requirement drafted
history.note: The trial worksheet shall distinguish an archive receipt from an approval record.

engineering.title: Each comparison cites its own archived source
fields: The comparison sheet shall identify the source of each example reference.
Open each citation on the comparison sheet. For a broken citation, identify the comparison without attributing it to a similarly named file.
Each indexed comparison resolves to a retained reference or states the gap.

history.title: Requirement baselined
history.note: The comparison sheet shall identify the source of each example reference.

engineering.title: Panel and carrier records use the same name for the orientation mark
fields: A reader using the carrier drawing and the panel record must be able to find the same orientation mark in the assembled view.
A reviewer can trace the same witness label through the carrier definition, panel interface record and retained assembled view.

history.title: Requirement recorded
history.note: The released carrier and panel records shall use the same named orientation witness to identify the assembled interface.

engineering.title: Witness label can be read with the guard in view
fields: The archived assembled view shall allow the identification witness to be read with the access guard in its documented configuration.
The view identifies the article and every part of its witness label required for record comparison.

history.title: Requirement recorded
history.note: The archived assembled view shall allow the identification witness to be read with the access guard in its documented configuration.

engineering.title: Permanent identifier on archived exports
fields: An archived recorder export shall identify its exact serialized article even if the working alias changes.
The export manifest records the serial from the signed handoff. If an alias is present, it appears as secondary information.

history.title: Requirement recorded
history.note: An archived recorder export shall identify its exact serialized article even if the working alias changes.

engineering.title: Comparison checklist names the design revision used for the article
fields: A reviewer must be able to find the design revision used for a comparison from the article’s checklist, even when two revisions share a packet title.
The retained packet resolves to the released Rev B definition for the identified article. Earlier packet versions remain available through their own archive references.

history.title: Requirement recorded
history.note: A comparison record shall identify the Engineering release in effect for the article it describes.

engineering.title: Inspection packet opens the approved receipt and keeps the earlier copy
fields: A reader reopening the packet must be able to tell which signed receipt was approved and retrieve the earlier one separately.
The active receipt has a source attribution and applicable revision. The superseded copy can be opened from its historical entry.

history.title: Requirement recorded
history.note: The inspection packet shall resolve to the approved source receipt and preserve any superseded receipt under a separate archive reference.

engineering.title: Archive records distinguish receipts, observations and approvals
fields: The research register shall distinguish an attachment receipt, an observation and an approved disposition.
The example index assigns each entry an explicit source and review state. Unavailable source records remain visible as gaps.

history.title: Requirement recorded
history.note: The research register shall distinguish an attachment receipt, an observation and an approved disposition.

fields: The witness image index shall identify the article and the record it accompanies.

history.title: Witness image belongs to the indexed article
history.note: The witness image index shall identify the article and the record it accompanies.

catalogEvidence.source: Demo bench archive · IG-E2 · desktop indicator, spacer-fitted lamp state card
catalogEvidence.observation: The left-only selection lights the left center without lighting the right center. A pale line on the right rim also appears in the both-off picture taken under the same room light.
catalogEvidence.supports: The rim alone is a poor indicator of an unintended electrical response. The center of each opening distinguishes the two selected states in this card.
catalogEvidence.followUp: Use the guide-movement images to assess the separate spill observed when the guide shifts.

build.title: Fitted a floating clip beside the display board’s outer segment

requirement.title: Keep the outer display segment visible as the board warms and cools

catalogEvidence.source: Demo bench archive · DC-E1 · desktop segment display, individual-segment worksheet
catalogEvidence.observation: The all-segments image makes the outer stroke look broken. With that segment selected on its own, lifting the removable mask exposes a continuous lit stroke. The neighboring segment stays dark.
catalogEvidence.supports: The comparison separates a hidden working segment from a missing segment response on this display board.
catalogEvidence.followUp: Keep the masked view beside this result when judging whether the assembled display is readable.

catalogEvidence.title: The bright line above the outer segment remains on a blank display

build.title: Fitted a floating clip beside the display board’s outer segment

requirement.title: Keep the outer display segment visible as the board warms and cools

catalogEvidence.source: Demo bench archive · DC-E2 · retained-mask display, illuminated and blank frame pair
catalogEvidence.observation: The outer stroke disappears when the blank pattern replaces the single-segment pattern. A slender line on the mask remains in both images, at the same point above the stroke.
catalogEvidence.supports: The line in this pair is independent of the selected display pattern. It is insufficient evidence that a second segment was powered.
catalogEvidence.followUp: Retain both patterns in the display reviewer’s comparison.

catalogEvidence.title: The last segment changes with the selected pattern behind the clear window

build.title: Built the clear-window carrier for the display card

requirement.title: Every display segment must remain distinguishable through the window

catalogEvidence.source: Demo bench archive · DW-E1 · tabletop display, bare card and clear-window pattern check
catalogEvidence.observation: The bare card and the windowed card each lose the same final stroke on the blank pattern, then show it again on the last-segment pattern. A reflected bar remains on the clear window in both blank views.
catalogEvidence.supports: The segment responds through the clear window in the recorded pair. The bar does not track the display state.
catalogEvidence.followUp: Compare the smoked-window view separately before selecting a window.

catalogEvidence.title: The green face stays lit after the reader loses its reply

build.title: Replaced the center clip with an offset clip on the bench enclosure

requirement.title: The indicator must reply with the enclosure lid open and closed

catalogEvidence.source: Demo bench archive · IC-E1 · desk indicator enclosure, an indicator face beside the reader state
catalogEvidence.observation: On the center-clip article the face remains green with the lid shut, although the reader marks the current selection unanswered. When the lid reopens, the next selection changes both the face and the reader label.
catalogEvidence.supports: A lit face can retain the last selection. It is insufficient evidence that the indicator is still responding.
catalogEvidence.followUp: Keep the new-selection response and the rear-port access observation separate.

build.title: Filed the corrected REF-FFLY-01 photo manifest

requirement.title: Witness image belongs to the indexed article

catalogEvidence.source: Demo bench archive · FF-WIT-E1 · witness-image reader, W1, W2 and empty-entry screen contact sheet
catalogEvidence.observation: The signed W2 entry shows the image with its matching corner mark. Selecting an empty entry clears the filename but leaves that same corner visible. Selecting W1 changes both the name and the corner.
catalogEvidence.supports: The unchanged preview on an empty entry cannot identify another witness image. The filename and the visible corner agree on the two populated entries.
catalogEvidence.followUp: Keep the selected entry and preview together when checking the handoff.

catalogEvidence.title: The attachment reader shows a green badge for a report with an empty image slot

build.title: Logged the report and its missing attachment

catalogEvidence.source: Demo bench archive · FF-ATT-E1 · attachment reader, report-only and empty-slot display check
catalogEvidence.observation: The report page opens and the green badge lights. The inspection slot still reads empty. Moving to an empty report entry turns the badge off without changing the inspection slot.
catalogEvidence.supports: The badge follows report availability in these two selections. It does not establish that the inspection attachment is present.
catalogEvidence.followUp: Use the individual attachment entry for the outstanding inspection handoff.

catalogEvidence.title: A held key advances the desk counter once; its release leaves the total unchanged

build.title: Compared two guard heights on the desktop counter

requirement.title: The counter must record a deliberate press and ignore a passing sleeve

catalogEvidence.source: Demo bench archive · BG-E1 · desk counter, held key and release worksheet
catalogEvidence.observation: With the raised guard the total changes on the recorded deliberate press. A later still shows the cap held down at the same count. The count remains there after release, and changes on the next deliberate press.
catalogEvidence.supports: The sheet distinguishes one recorded press from repeated counting while held. It says nothing about incidental contact.
catalogEvidence.followUp: Use the sleeve-brush comparison separately when choosing the guard.

catalogEvidence.title: Unplugging the left lamp darkens it while its last port name remains on screen

build.title: Fitted the keyed collar to the two-port lamp reader

requirement.title: Lamp readbacks must identify the correct port without trapping either plug

catalogEvidence.source: Demo bench archive · PK-E1 · two-lamp tabletop reader, unplugged and relabeled states
catalogEvidence.observation: With the keyed collars fitted the left selection lights the left lamp. In the unplugged view that lamp is dark and the right lamp is dark, but the reader still displays the previous left-port caption.
catalogEvidence.supports: A retained caption identifies the last selection. It does not establish a current lamp response or a fault in the other socket.
catalogEvidence.followUp: Keep the lamp and caption in the same frame when assessing the keyed pair.

catalogEvidence.title: The input label stays on B after disconnection, but its activity dot goes out

build.title: Separated the printed input legend from the reader channel check

catalogEvidence.source: Demo bench archive · RC-E1 · two-input tabletop reader, last label and activity dot
catalogEvidence.observation: The connected B view shows a B label beside a bright dot. In the disconnected picture the label stays B and the dot is dark. The next A selection changes the label and lights its own dot.
catalogEvidence.supports: The dot carries information about activity that the retained label does not. This card covers one change of selection.
catalogEvidence.followUp: Compare both indications before closing the disconnected-display question.

catalogEvidence.title: The seated indicator holds the previous mark as the reference starts to fall

build.title: Fitted a spring seat in the display’s loose probe pocket

requirement.title: The desk display must follow the reference on warming and cooling

catalogEvidence.source: Demo bench archive · SP-E1 · desk indicator, spring-seat cooling and settled readout sheet
catalogEvidence.observation: In the return sheet the reference is already below its warm mark while the display still shows the earlier reading. The two agree again at the final settled entry. The spring-seat warming sheet stopped before this interval.
catalogEvidence.supports: Agreement after settling does not establish that the indicator followed the falling reference throughout.
catalogEvidence.followUp: Keep the warming and cooling sheets together for the pocket design review.

catalogEvidence.title: The reader stores the neighboring swatch as white where glare crosses its edge

build.title: Built opaque and vented shades for the swatch reader

requirement.title: Keep the reference patch visible without masking the adjoining swatch

catalogEvidence.source: Demo bench archive · SS-E1 · tabletop swatch reader, bright edge and held-preview comparison
catalogEvidence.observation: With the vented shade the bright edge appears white in the live preview and in the held sample. The corresponding strip in the reference card remains pale blue. The middle of the swatch stays blue in all three.
catalogEvidence.supports: The loss is already present in the reader preview. Saving the frame does not recover the edge color.
catalogEvidence.followUp: Compare the center and edge patches when assessing the shade against the reference.

catalogEvidence.title: Selecting an empty socket leaves the previous camera image in the preview

build.title: Fitted a keyed insert to the camera reader jig

requirement.title: Selecting the left socket must return the left camera image

catalogEvidence.source: Demo bench archive · CK-E1 · two-socket image reader, keyed insert and empty-port selection
catalogEvidence.observation: Reading the left and right reference cards returns their own pictures with the keyed insert. After the right camera is removed, selecting right darkens the input indicator but retains the last right-hand picture.
catalogEvidence.supports: The keyed guide addresses a swap between connected inputs. A retained image is insufficient to identify a connected camera.
catalogEvidence.followUp: Use the input indicator alongside the preview for empty-port handoffs.

catalogEvidence.title: The left key’s lamp goes dark on release before the right key lights

build.title: Replaced the guide edge that caught the neighboring switch key

requirement.title: One key selection must return only that key’s label

catalogEvidence.source: Demo bench archive · FG-E1 · tabletop two-key pad, selected-key lamp and release sheet
catalogEvidence.observation: The flush guide returns the two key labels separately. In the face photographs the left lamp goes dark between touches; the next right touch lights only the right lamp. The raised-edge comparison lacks a release view.
catalogEvidence.supports: The observed release separates two complete selections on the flush guide. It adds no release result for the earlier guide.
catalogEvidence.followUp: Keep the lamp sequence beside the original key-label comparison.

catalogEvidence.title: Clearing the selected cell leaves the last highlight on the preview grid

build.title: Replaced the rotatable grid with a keyed overlay

requirement.title: The overlay grid must identify the selected corner cell

catalogEvidence.source: Demo bench archive · OG-E1 · tabletop checkerboard display, corner selection and cleared grid
catalogEvidence.observation: The keyed overlay registers both corner selections correctly. After the selector clears, the corner label empties, but the last corner stays lit until another cell is selected.
catalogEvidence.supports: The overlay locates populated selections accurately. The persistent highlight does not identify a current choice on a cleared grid.
catalogEvidence.followUp: Include the cleared selector when reviewing empty-grid behavior.

catalogEvidence.title: The face lamp moves to B before the readout changes from A

build.title: Fitted the detent plate to the recorder’s input selector

catalogEvidence.source: Demo bench archive · SD-E1 · desktop input selector, face-lamp and readout worksheet

catalogEvidence.supports: The lamp and readout can disagree in an intermediate view. The sheet cannot measure how long that lasts.
catalogEvidence.followUp: Retain the intermediate still when deciding which indication identifies a settled selection.

projects.title: Odin
projects.description: AstroForge launched Odin to photograph asteroid 2022 OB5. Dawn identifies SatDrive aboard the spacecraft.

projects.title: Firefly constellation
projects.description: Pixxel’s Firefly satellites image Earth in many narrow wavelength bands to study vegetation and water quality. Dawn identifies SatDrive on three Fireflies. The demo separates the W2 label proof for REF-FFLY-01 from the padded-lid packet for REF-FFLY-02. Both use the same integration revision.

projects.title: Pulse · ION Laurentius
projects.description: D-Orbit’s Laurentius carrier deployed satellites for the Pulse mission and hosted demonstration payloads. D-Orbit identifies Dawn’s propulsion aboard the carrier, SCV002.

projects.title: LizzieSat platform
projects.description: LizzieSat is Sidus Space’s platform for instruments including remote-sensing payloads. Sidus selected Dawn to supply propulsion for the platform.

projects.title: Lunar data relay satellites
projects.description: Two planned satellites would relay data between Earth and a lunar lander. Blue Canyon designs the satellite platforms and integrates the communications payloads. Dawn announced it would supply propulsion.

projects.title: Lunar navigation satellite
projects.description: ArkEdge is developing a satellite for positioning around the Moon. Its agreement with Dawn covers SatDrive for one spacecraft in the wider lunar navigation program.

projects.title: Docking demonstration
projects.description: Aule Space plans to demonstrate spacecraft docking as part of its work on extending satellite life. Dawn announced a SatDrive supply contract for the demonstration.

projects.title: Refuellable spacecraft platform study
projects.description: CNES asked Dawn, Infinite Orbits and Exotrail to study two representative spacecraft platforms. The study compared what would have to change for each to receive fuel in orbit.

projects.title: ENOS
projects.description: Reditus designed ENOS Mk1 to host microgravity research and manufacturing experiments. Dawn announced it would supply SatDrive for ENOS.

projects.title: Oasis Beta
projects.description: Tumbleweed plans to return research samples from orbit on Oasis Beta. Its agreement with Dawn covers propulsion for that mission.

projects.title: Aurora spaceplane program
projects.description: Dawn is developing a reusable suborbital aircraft to carry research instruments. Experiment teams can recover their payload after a flight and revise it for a later one. In this demo, the Flight 57 exhibit card has separate labels for the flight date and the date of the announcement.

projects.title: Loop Network
projects.description: Dawn’s proposed Loop Network would let satellites receive fuel in orbit. Its docking and fluid-transfer interface is cataloged separately.

projects.title: OSSIE
projects.description: UARX Space selected Dawn as propulsion supplier for OSSIE. Dawn reports the vehicle launched with SatDrive and its docking port.

projects.title: Hiber Three
projects.description: Dawn’s flight announcement identifies its propulsion aboard the Hiber Three satellite.

projects.title: GEOryder
projects.description: The GEOryder consortium is developing a reusable carrier for small satellites headed to geostationary orbit. Infinite Orbits leads the program and Dawn contributes propulsion work.

systems.title: SatDrive
systems.description: Dawn’s family of satellite propulsion systems. The catalog groups bench fixtures by project integration. Each fixture has its own serial and comparison results. For example, the Odin enclosure and the Firefly label fixture have different evidence registers. Their REF serials identify demo articles.

systems.title: OSSIE docking interface
systems.description: UARX selected the structural version of Dawn’s docking port for OSSIE. This entry covers the mechanical docking interface on the spacecraft.

systems.title: ION SCV002 Laurentius
systems.description: D-Orbit calls this satellite carrier Laurentius. SCV002 is the carrier identifier used in Dawn’s flight account.

systems.title: LizzieSat
systems.description: Sidus Space selected Dawn to supply propulsion for its LizzieSat platform. The catalog records the platform agreement without assigning it to an individual satellite.

systems.title: Oasis Beta
systems.description: Tumbleweed is developing Oasis Beta to return research samples from orbit. Its agreement with Dawn covers propulsion for Beta.

systems.title: Aurora spaceplane
systems.description: Dawn’s reusable suborbital research aircraft carries experiments. The Aurora project includes the vehicle and its research program. REF-AURORA-01 identifies the demo bench display; the historical flight entries have flight numbers of their own.

systems.title: Docking and Fluid Transfer interface
systems.description: Dawn’s docking and fluid-transfer interface for the planned Loop Network. The catalog records the interface design at system level.

systems.title: Hiber Three
systems.description: Dawn identified Hiber Three by name in its March 2021 flight announcement. Hiber describes it as one of its second-generation satellites.

systems.title: GEOryder vehicle
systems.description: A carrier under development to transport small satellites to geostationary orbit. The design is intended for repeated use.

systems.title: Mānuka locator coupons
systems.description: Two coupons represent different locator designs. In the photographs, the mark on the fixed coupon identifies its reference face. The adjustable coupon has a separate reference face.

systems.title: Optical payload integration kit
systems.description: The tray and detector cover have labels that must stay visible when assembled. On the HI-006 bench enclosure, moving the cable clip off the hinged lid kept the readout working with the lid open and closed.

systems.title: Survey payload panel
systems.description: The panel carrier has an ID tag and a separate mark for orientation. In the RM-012 tabletop comparison the lip hides a rim arrow. A face arrow stays visible, but glare with the cover fitted is still an open question.

systems.title: Kōtare mapping payload
systems.description: On the KM-201 map display, a loose overlay could rotate and put a highlighted square one cell off its target. A keyed overlay aligned both corner selections with the reference grid.

systems.title: Kea integration carrier
systems.description: The Kea carrier holds a mounting bracket behind a cover. Rev A checks bracket fit and fastener access. A separate LK-021 bench comparison shows how a guide edge can catch the neighboring key and register both keys at once.

systems.title: Tern payload cradle
systems.description: The TC-003 tabletop cradle rocked on opposite feet until a compliant foot seated all four corners. On TC-011, the open question is how much of the inspection mark can be seen through the guard.

systems.title: Weka data recorder
systems.description: Two recordings made on WR-101 contain different sample sequences. Selecting a recording by the recorder name can replay the wrong sequence. The bench comparison checks selection by the original recording reference.

systems.title: Survey instrument node
systems.description: On the PU-012 desk display, a loose probe lags the reference as it warms. With the spring seat fitted, the display follows the reference on warming. The cooling trace is still missing.

systems.title: Kiwi imagery payload
systems.description: Two identical sockets on the KA-002 camera-reader jig can return the wrong image. A keyed guide distinguishes left from right. The Rev B archive keeps each unit’s image manifest and signed cover separately.

systems.title: Kākā relay recorder
systems.description: The KR-011 desk recorder could alternate between inputs with its selector between labels. The fitted plate holds the selector in distinct positions. The recorded comparison covers this unit.

systems.title: Mātātā spectral payload
systems.description: Two shades on the MS-001 color reader have different drawbacks. The reference patch darkened behind the opaque shade as it warmed. With the vented shade, glare made the adjacent patch harder to distinguish.

systems.title: Miro payload inspection interface
systems.description: The MP-002 bench jig holds a label card for inspection. A second pin kept both corner marks aligned after movement. Whether the card comes out easily with both pins in place remains open.

systems.title: Rātā image comparison archive
systems.description: Different source images can reach the comparison software with the same filename. The RL-011 comparison checks whether the original frame reference puts the correct images side by side and leaves a frame without a match visible.

auroraFlightComments.body: The wingtip photo and its tighter crop show the same instant. Keep the wider frame when comparing where the camera was looking.
auroraFlightComments.author: Camera reviewer

auroraFlightComments.body: In the demo viewing copy of Flight 50, the wide shot cuts straight to a close-up. I marked the cut on the viewing sheet so the next reviewer does not time the missing interval.
auroraFlightComments.author: Campaign reviewer

auroraFlightComments.body: Use the campaign report for the date of the morning flight. The publication date is also on the page and is easy to mistake for the flight date.
auroraFlightComments.author: Archive editor

auroraFlightComments.body: The afternoon footage belongs with Flight 56. It helps to put it next to the morning entry when reading the two-flight campaign report.
auroraFlightComments.author: Campaign reviewer

auroraFlightComments.body: The edit changes camera angles during the climb. The report is the better place to cite the milestone; the film shows what the cameras captured.
auroraFlightComments.author: Archive editor

auroraFlightComments.body: I can see the contrast change across the infrared image. Without a scale in the same frame I would describe the pattern rather than quote a value.
auroraFlightComments.author: Camera reviewer

auroraFlightComments.body: The last image in this sequence is missing. I would leave a gap in the contact sheet rather than repeat the preceding image.
auroraFlightComments.author: Campaign reviewer

auroraFlightComments.body: The review sheet starts with the runway already in view. I marked the first frame of the excerpt so the next editor can find the same picture in the compilation.
auroraFlightComments.author: Edit assistant

auroraFlightComments.body: The contact print is turned a quarter turn from the review copy. The notch in the border sits beside the same corner in both. Keep that border in the next print.
auroraFlightComments.author: Image reviewer

auroraFlightComments.body: The two prints on this page are labeled 52/53 as a pair. The first one includes the flight number from the film. The second has only the campaign caption, so I left it with the campaign.
auroraFlightComments.author: Archive editor

auroraFlightComments.body: The right wing is visible at the edge of the wide print and disappears in the square crop. Only the wide print answers the question we had about which side the camera shows.
auroraFlightComments.author: Camera reviewer

auroraFlightComments.body: There is a pale line down the right side of the paper proof. It disappears when I open the same frame on the review monitor. I marked the print for replacement.
auroraFlightComments.author: Imaging technician

auroraFlightComments.body: The handwritten time beside the runway still is the time it was copied. The reader who filed it left the event-time box blank. Keep the two fields separate when indexing the scan.
auroraFlightComments.author: Media librarian

auroraFlightComments.body: Two items on the bench return slip both say “recorder.” The flight case contains the recorder body; the small pouch contains its card reader. I have listed them on separate lines.
auroraFlightComments.author: Payload support

auroraFlightComments.body: The full sheet includes the legend beside the image. Our small binder copy loses its last line at the fold. Please leave the full sheet open for anyone comparing the colors.
auroraFlightComments.author: Print reviewer

auroraFlightComments.body: I checked the paired print against the folder list. The blank square on the right has no corresponding file. It belongs in the contact sheet as a gap, with the next pair on its original row.

programs.title: ION Satellite Carrier
programs.description: D-Orbit operates ION carriers for in-orbit transportation. Dawn identifies its propulsion equipment on the first nine carriers.

programs.title: Hiber Four
programs.description: Hiber launched its second-generation communications satellite in January 2021. Dawn’s CTO identified the propulsion unit it supplied.

programs.title: TOM formation
programs.description: TOM-1, TOM-2 and TOM-3 observed an ash cloud over Anak Krakatau. ZfT identifies Dawn as the propulsion supplier for all three spacecraft.

programs.title: GITAI SC1

sources.title: GITAI · SC1 equipment declaration to the FCC

programs.title: Alén Space navigation program
programs.description: Dawn reports two CubeDrive systems for Alén Space’s positioning, navigation and timing work. Its heritage chart does not name the spacecraft.

flights.title: Aurora’s first five flights
flights.summary: Aurora first flew with jet engines. Over three days at Glentanner, the team flew the same airframe five times. Two flights took place within 90 minutes of each other. These flights are included in the 47-flight jet phase.

flights.title: Wingtip photograph from the first jet campaign
flights.summary: The campaign gallery identifies its wingtip image as flight 3. The release dates the five-flight campaign but leaves the individual photograph undated.

flights.title: Jet-powered airframe trials
flights.summary: Dawn’s 2024 campaign report and its later flight log count 47 jet-powered flights. The final training included repeated landing trials. The Phase 1 film gave a total of 48 at the time. Dawn does not reconcile the two counts.

flights.title: Two jet flights before lunch
flights.summary: Dawn’s Wednesday campaign update records two Monday flights before lunch. The report groups the flights together and does not give their individual numbers or the total for the campaign.

flights.title: First rocket-powered campaign
flights.summary: Starting on 29 March, Dawn flew the same aircraft three times in three days. The earlier jet-powered trials had used the same airframe.

flights.title: First flight on rocket power
flights.summary: The aircraft that had flown the jet trials took off from Glentanner on rocket power for the first time. Dawn’s 2023 film documents the changeover.

flights.title: Second day of the Glentanner campaign
flights.summary: The aircraft flew on the middle day of the three-day campaign. Dawn labels the short onboard excerpt as flight 49 in its compilation.

flights.title: Final flight of the first rocket campaign
flights.summary: Dawn released a separate film of the third flight and identified it as flight 50. Its publication marks the end of this campaign before the next airframe updates.

flights.title: Three flights at Glentanner
flights.summary: Aurora returned to Glentanner for three flights in late July. Dawn’s contemporary campaign report identifies flight 53 as the last of the three and publishes photographs from aboard the aircraft.

flights.title: Flight 51 onboard footage
flights.summary: Dawn’s later film labels the onboard view as flight 51. The contemporary July report identifies flight 53 as the last of three flights, placing 51 in that campaign by sequence. Its day is unpublished.

flights.title: Flight 52 camera excerpt
flights.summary: Dawn labels the camera excerpt as flight 52. It falls by sequence within the July campaign, which ended with flight 53. The film gives no day for this recording.

flights.title: Last flight of the July campaign
flights.summary: Dawn published the aircraft’s onboard film from the third flight of its July campaign. Its dated photo captions identify this as flight 53.

flights.title: Flight 54 runway camera excerpt
flights.summary: Dawn’s film cuts to a runway view labeled flight 54. The clip identifies the flight without dating it or naming a payload.

flights.title: Aurora photographed in flight
flights.summary: The first of two flights that day supplied the airborne photograph Dawn later used to introduce Aurora to customers. The campaign report identifies both flights.

flights.title: Aurora’s onboard views of Aoraki
flights.summary: The afternoon flight supplied the footage for Dawn’s music film over Aoraki / Mount Cook. Its 99-minute running time is the length of the edit.

flights.title: Two flights in one day
flights.summary: Dawn’s original report dates flights 55 and 56 to 27 September. Its later retrospective gives 4 October, the date of the original announcement.

flights.title: First supersonic flight
flights.summary: Aurora became the first aircraft designed and built in New Zealand to break the sound barrier. Dawn reported Mach 1.1 and a peak altitude of 82,500 feet on flight 57. The team identified the aircraft’s behavior as it crossed the speed of sound as the last major technical risk for the program.

flights.title: Two flights on the supersonic flight day
flights.summary: Dawn’s film account says Aurora flew again six hours after flight 57. It gives no flight number for the afternoon departure.

flights.title: Flight 58 runway camera excerpt
flights.summary: Dawn labels this camera view as flight 58 in the 15-flight compilation. The sequence shows the runway and mountains, without giving a day for the footage.

flights.title: Pathfinder research payloads
flights.summary: Dawn groups Cal Poly’s student recorder, ASU’s infrared imager and the Johns Hopkins APL payload under Pathfinder. Its program lists Scout Space separately.

flights.site: Tāwhaki National Aerospace Centre, New Zealand
flights.title: Cal Poly student payload
flights.summary: Cal Poly students flew an off-the-shelf data recorder to find out how it compared with a custom system. They handed the payload to Dawn in March. The university later published the path reconstructed from its recordings of the June flight, Aurora’s first from Tāwhaki.

artifacts.label: Flight path recorded by Cal Poly’s payload

flights.site: Tāwhaki National Aerospace Centre, New Zealand
flights.title: ASU thermal-infrared imager
flights.summary: ASU flew a compact version of a planetary infrared camera to see what it could capture during a recoverable Earth-observation flight. LEO-TIMS recorded from before takeoff through landing. The team retrieved the instrument and published images of clouds, sea and coastline.

flights.site: Tāwhaki National Aerospace Centre, New Zealand
flights.title: Scout Space payload flight
flights.summary: Scout Space’s Morning Sparrow payload flew aboard Aurora. Dawn identifies Scout as the first commercial operator to fly a payload on the aircraft.

flights.site: Tāwhaki National Aerospace Centre, New Zealand
flights.title: Johns Hopkins APL research payload
flights.summary: Johns Hopkins APL flew a data acquisition payload. Dawn later released a film placing two onboard views side by side. Its flight history identifies this as flight 62 without giving the exact day.

flights.site: Tāwhaki National Aerospace Centre, New Zealand
flights.title: DARTE campaign · flights 63 and 64
flights.summary: Aurora flew twice from Tāwhaki during the DARTE campaign. Dawn’s public history records the flights together and identifies the month.
